title: Snorkel AI triples valuation to $3.5B as demand for AI training data booms
slides: Snorkel AI now valued at $3.5B, but why?
Demand for AI training data is booming.
Data labeling is shifting to programmatic synthesis, not humans.
Your models may soon run on synthetic data, changing accuracy.
Test one model on synthetic data today to see if it holds.
thread_text:
1. The $3.5B Question

Snorkel AI just hit a $3.5B valuation. But here's the twist: the company is betting that humans won't be the ones labeling data for much longer.

2. The Data Gold Rush

Every AI model needs millions of labeled examples. Until recently, that meant hiring armies of people to tag images, text, and audio. That demand is still exploding.

3. Goodbye, Humans?

Snorkel's core bet: programmatic synthesis. Instead of paying humans to label, you write code that generates labeled data automatically. Faster, cheaper, and scalable.

4. When Synthetic Data Bites Back

But synthetic data can introduce subtle biases and blind spots. Your model may ace the synthetic test set and fail on real-world inputs. Accuracy isn't guaranteed.

5. Test It Yourself

Grab one of your models and retrain it on a small synthetic dataset. Compare its accuracy on real data. If the gap is big, you've found your next problem.
